clue.text: Reserve able to control movements in very large area

blocks.note: a sub is a reserve player on the bench
continent describes someone able to control their bowel and bladder movements

explanation.surface: A substitute player who is good at controlling the play across a wide area of the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movements' suggests sport or dance, but here it means bodily movements, the medical sense of continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A subcontinent is a huge landmass forming part of a continent, such as India.

clue.text: Sensitive issue excited open riots

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so the letters get jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A touchy subject that has sparked rioting in the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: A sore point is a topic that upsets someone whenever it is raised, like a tender spot.

clue.text: Inferior jewellery is a bit gauche

blocks.note: bum is slang for poor quality, as in a bum deal
bling is showy jewellery

explanation.surface: Wearing cheap, flashy jewellery is in rather poor taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumbling describes clumsy, awkward behaviour, close in sense to slightly gauche or ungainly.

clue.text: Start off unprepared? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: tells us to swap each of the preceding words for its antonym

blocks.note: the opposite of off
the opposite of unprepared is ready, or set

explanation.surface: Someone sets out on a task without getting ready, and is told the reverse is true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' reads as a phrase, but only Start is the definition; off and unprepared are each flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its beginning, as in the onset of winter.

clue.text: They perform plays initially in ramshackle shanties

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
something ramshackle is falling apart, so the letters are disordered
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
first letter of plays

explanation.surface: Actors putting on plays in tumbledown huts.
explanation.definitionFit: Thespians are actors, named after Thespis, the legendary first actor of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Knock over stone cask to get spice

indicators.note: knocking something over turns it upside down, so in a down clue the letters read backwards

blocks.note: a precious stone
a tun is a large barrel for wine or beer

explanation.surface: Tipping over a stone barrel to get at the spice stored inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is the aromatic seed of an evergreen tree, grated as a culinary spice.

clue.text: Inlay carved regularly from this material

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every second one

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A craftsman's inlay was carved out of some particular substance.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also works as a description, since mother-of-pearl is commonly carved for inlays.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is mother-of-pearl, the iridescent lining of shells used as a decorative substance.

clue.text: Gets rid of Charlie's chickens

blocks.note: first meaning: throws away
Chuck is a nickname for Charles, so Charlie's is a third reading
second meaning: chuck is a dialect word for a chicken

explanation.surface: Someone disposes of the hens belonging to a man called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie looks like C from the phonetic alphabet, but here it is a name: Chuck is the American nickname for Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: To chuck is informally to discard, and chuck is also a regional or childish name for a hen.

clue.text: Half scrambling is something you can do with an egg

definitions.text: something you can do with an egg

blocks.note: first meaning: the first half of scrambling is scram, slang for go away

blocks.clueFragment: something you can do with an egg
blocks.note: second meaning: whisking an egg with a fork

explanation.walkthrough: Scrambling and egg suggest cooking throughout, but the first half of scrambling is the slang word scram, which is the expression's other meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is slang for leave quickly, the same as scram, and you beat an egg when whisking it.

clue.text: Women's section starts to have arts review every month

indicators.note: starts points to the opening letter of each word that follows

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A women's group in a club begins reviewing the arts once a month.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the separate quarters of a Muslim household reserved for women.

clue.text: Spot equipment getting picked up for display

indicators.note: picked up as on a radio or by the ear, meaning the words are heard spoken

blocks.note: a speck is a spot, tackle is equipment

explanation.surface: Noticing some gear being collected for an exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking public show or visual display put on for an audience.

clue.text: Seize one chance to have joint control

blocks.note: to cop is slang for to catch or seize
Roman numeral one
a lot is a chance, as in drawing lots

explanation.surface: Grabbing an opportunity to share the controls of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' could suggest cannabis, but it means shared, as when two pilots fly together.
explanation.definitionFit: To copilot is to share flying duties as the second pilot, splitting the controls.

clue.text: Check before discharge

blocks.note: the prefix pre- means before
to vent is to let out or release

explanation.surface: A doctor checks a patient over before they are released from hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to stop or halt it, which is to stop it happening.

clue.text: Research facility is abandoning inaccessible treatment

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the small word is dropped from the longer one
treatment suggests processing or working over, so the letters get reworked

blocks.note: the longer word
taken as written and removed

explanation.surface: A medical research centre gives up on a treatment that patients cannot reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A science lab is a laboratory, a workplace equipped for experiments and research.

clue.text: Clear old boyfriend on single charge

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
single means one
a rate is a fee or charge

explanation.surface: A former boyfriend is cleared of a lone criminal charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' reads as an accusation, which suits clearing someone, but it is a price.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to free someone from blame, declaring them innocent of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Fight to have water source back

indicators.note: back means the letters run in the backwards direction

blocks.note: taps supply water

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out over getting the water supply restored.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel or minor squabble between people.

clue.text: Loving lots of people providing fantastic playroom above yard

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters are rearranged freely

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: Someone with many lovers gets a fabulous playroom over the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, above means the first piece is placed on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyamory is the practice of having several romantic relationships at once, with everyone's consent.

clue.text: Doubled up per diem to produce boring talk

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters climb, so they read backwards

blocks.note: per diem is Latin for a day, or each day
doubled means the same piece is written a second time

explanation.surface: An employee's daily allowance is doubled and it leads only to dull chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: Per diem usually means a daily expense allowance, but here it is just its Latin translation.
explanation.definitionFit: Yada yada is an informal phrase for tedious, predictable chatter, like blah blah.

clue.text: Meter maid is grim dictator at heart

indicators.note: heart points to the central letters of each word

blocks.note: the middle two letters of grim
the middle two letters of dictator

explanation.surface: A traffic warden who is a cruel tyrant underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: Lovely Rita, the Beatles song, is about a meter maid, a woman who issues parking tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: Rita is the parking warden celebrated in the Beatles song Lovely Rita, Meter Maid.

clue.text: Try again to bring up having ambassador arrested

indicators.note: having something means holding it, so one piece goes inside another
arrested means held captive, confirming one piece is locked within the other

blocks.note: to rear a child is to bring it up
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A court decides to retry a case raising the arrest of a diplomat.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehear a case in court is to try it a second time before judges.

clue.text: Fool was confused by overturned vote? That's rubbish

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are muddled
overturned means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to cod is old slang for to hoax or fool
the letters to rearrange
a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: An idiot was baffled when the election result was reversed, and dismisses it as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Cod meaning to fool is old British slang, still seen in cod as an adjective for fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Codswallop is British slang for nonsense, the stuff people dismiss as garbage.

clue.text: Too much entered for each craftsman

indicators.note: something that has entered has gone inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: per means for each
OTT is short for over the top

explanation.surface: An overpriced entry fee charged for every craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A potter is an artisan who shapes clay into pots and ceramics.

clue.text: Cheer on opera star, one who appeared naked

blocks.note: Go! is shouted to urge someone on
a diva is a leading female opera singer

explanation.surface: Fans cheering a prima donna who once performed in the nude.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Godiva, by legend, rode naked through Coventry streets to protest her husband's taxes.

clue.text: Successful record in register

blocks.note: a hit is a chart-topping record
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A chart-topping single gets listed in an official record book.
explanation.definitionFit: When a remark hits home it registers, making its full impact felt by the listener.

clue.text: Article that oddly describes character from Athens

indicators.note: oddly means keeping the letters in odd-numbered positions

blocks.note: the definite article
first and third letters of that

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece profiles an unusual person from the Greek capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person, but it means a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, so a written character used in Athens.

clue.text: Clear reprimand when spades lost by worker

indicators.note: lost means gone missing, so a letter goes

blocks.note: to blast someone is to tell them off
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
a worker ant

explanation.surface: An unmistakable telling-off when a labourer misplaces the shovels.
explanation.walkthrough: Spades suggests digging tools in the surface, but it is the card suit, abbreviated S.
explanation.definitionFit: Something blatant is obvious and unashamed, plain for everyone to see.

clue.text: Party can make one negative

blocks.note: to make, as in she will make a good mother, is to be
a means one
no is a negative answer

explanation.surface: A celebration has the power to put a person in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: A beano is a British informal word for a lively party or celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is old British slang for a festive spree or celebratory get-together.

clue.text: Ace airman moving stuff from the US

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so the letters change places

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A top pilot is relocating his belongings from the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana are artefacts and memorabilia typical of American culture and history.

clue.text: Love a noted couple

blocks.note: taken as written
do and re are two notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Being fond of a famous pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' looks like famous, but it means made of musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to worship or cherish them deeply.

clue.text: Literary lady makes change after mob made a mess

indicators.note: a mess is a disordered jumble, so those letters are scrambled
after sends the word before it to the end, behind the rearranged letters

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
to vary is to change

explanation.surface: A woman of letters pushes for reform after a rioting crowd causes chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame Bovary is Flaubert's novel and its heroine Emma, a famous woman of fiction.
